claims.text: The Pulumi for Terraform Users guide covers how to reference existing Terraform state files from Pulumi, use any Terraform provider in Pulumi programs, import and use Terraform modules directly, convert HCL code to Pulumi, and orchestrate both Terraform and Pulumi deployments together.
Any Terraform provider can be used in Pulumi programs.
Terraform modules can be imported and used directly from Pulumi.
A Pulumi `StackReference` (`new pulumi.StackReference("core-infra")` with `getOutput("vpcId")`) can be used to consume outputs from a core infrastructure stack that 'could be Terraform'.

The `terraform.state.S3Reference` class (from `@pulumi/terraform`, also referenced as `pulumi.terraform.state.S3Reference`) exists and accepts `bucket` and `key` arguments to reference Terraform state stored in S3.
`terraform.state.S3Reference` objects expose a `getOutput(name)` method that returns outputs from the Terraform state (e.g., `private_subnet_ids`, `security_group_ids`, `kms_key_id`, `cluster_name`).
The `aws.ecs.Cluster` resource accepts a `configuration.executeCommandConfiguration` argument with `kmsKeyId` and `logging` (value `"DEFAULT"`) properties.
`pulumi import` can be used to bring Terraform-managed resources under Pulumi management.
State ownership can be transferred gradually, resource-by-resource, from Terraform to Pulumi during migration.

The command `pulumi import <type-token> <name> <id>` (e.g., `pulumi import aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc main-vpc vpc-12345`, `aws:ec2/subnet:Subnet`, `aws:ecs/cluster:Cluster`) is valid syntax for importing existing resources into Pulumi with these AWS type tokens.
Pulumi provides an 'import API' that can be used programmatically to import resources (as referenced in the migration helper comment).
Pulumi policies (Policy as Code) can enforce infrastructure policies that work across both Terraform and Pulumi resources.
The `@pulumi/policy` package exports `PolicyPack` and `validateResourceOfType`, and `new PolicyPack(name, { policies: [...] })` is the correct constructor form.

Pulumi policy definitions accept `name`, `description`, `enforcementLevel` (value `"mandatory"`), and `validateResource` properties, and `validateResourceOfType(resourceClass, (resource, args, reportViolation) => ...)` is the correct callback signature.
The `aws.s3.Bucket` resource has an `acl` property that can take the values `public-read` and `public-read-write`.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `tags` property accessible in policy validation as `instance.tags`.
The Automation API lets you embed Pulumi in applications for dynamic infrastructure management.

The Automation API is imported from `@pulumi/pulumi/automation`, and `pulumi.LocalWorkspace.createOrSelectStack({ stackName, projectName, program })` is a valid call for creating or selecting a stack with an inline program.
The `terraform` namespace is accessible as `pulumi.terraform` when importing `* as pulumi from "@pulumi/pulumi/automation"`.
The Automation API `Stack` object provides `setConfig(key, { value })`, and `up({ onOutput })` returns a result with an `outputs` property.
Pulumi component resources can integrate with Terraform behind the scenes, leaving the complexity of multi-tool management to the platform team rather than development teams.
Custom components extend `pulumi.ComponentResource`, call `super(type, name, {}, opts)`, and use `this.registerOutputs({...})` to register outputs.
The `@pulumi/terraform` package exports a `terraform.state` namespace with `S3Reference`.

`aws.lb.LoadBalancer`, `aws.ecs.TaskDefinition` (with `requiresCompatibilities`, `networkMode`, `cpu`, `memory`, `containerDefinitions`), and `aws.ecs.Service` (with `launchType`, `networkConfiguration.assignPublicIp`) accept the arguments shown in the example.
With this component pattern, developers can create WebApplications in Pulumi without knowing they depend on Terraform-managed resources.
